args.content:
# Stage 5 prototype PCB layout

Status: Reviewable first draft, 2026-10-08. No board has been fabricated or physically tested. The fresh v16 native run_drc result is clean for the stage's placement/routing checks, with four separately reported library-internal J1 hole_clearance findings still present. The current ERC and BOM/PINOUT drift results are clean. A fresh independent read-only KiCad JSON check confirms 0 unconnected items on the unchanged current board; its four intrinsic J1 errors remain disclosed below. Neither this draft nor its software checks establish manufacturing readiness or electrical qualification.

## Draft layout bounds

Stage 5 draft geometry is a 40 x 30 mm rectangle from (100,100) to (140,130), with F.Cu/B.Cu and nominal board thickness 1.6 mm. The original 1 oz copper and FR-4 fabrication requirements remain mandatory; no detailed copper-weight stackup or fabricator process has been verified. The implemented draft has 55 track segments and eight through vias, with no copper zones. Main power/return trunks are 0.8 mm wide; short power/ground escapes are 0.4-0.5 mm; CC and LED_A tracks are 0.25 mm. Via diameter/drill pairs are 0.6/0.3, 0.7/0.3 and 0.8/0.4 mm. These are provisional routing choices, not certified normal/fault-current or thermal ratings.

Rationale: retain the original envelope and accessible two-layer prototype while documenting what the board encodes and what fabrication must still establish.

All ten schematic footprints, physical pad geometry and pad-net assignments are retained. Only move_footprint moved/rotated parts; anchored edits changed the outline, traces, vias, board legends and reference-label positions. No footprint, pad or net was added, removed or rewritten. No schematic/BOM component value, current budget or device choice changed. MCU strapping, RTC and antenna constraints remain inapplicable because no MCU/radio is fitted. No ESD device was added; the documented absence of a TVS and unqualified ESD immunity are unchanged.

## Placement and component-side polarity

Coordinates below are footprint origins in mm, X right and Y down; rotations are absolute KiCad rotations on the front/component side.

| Refdes | X | Y | Rotation | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| J1 | 107 | 126.325 | 0 | USB mouth at the bottom edge; the installed footprint's PCB Edge drawing line is at Y=130. |
| J2 | 134 | 106 | 180 | Wire entry faces the top edge; inset preserves the library silkscreen and leaves wire/screw access for physical review. |
| J3 | 135.2 | 117 | 0 | Vertical header close to the right edge, separate from USB and terminal access. |
| U1 | 117 | 118 | 180 | IN/EN face the USB side, OUT faces the protected distribution side. |
| C1 | 113 | 118 | 90 | Input bypass adjacent to U1; input-side trace about 2.88 mm, with return-loop improvement still needed. |
| C2 | 121 | 118.95 | 0 | Output bypass adjacent to U1; OUT-to-C2 positive-pad trace about 2.09 mm. |
| R1 | 105.75 | 119.5 | 90 | Short separate CC1 escape. |
| R2 | 108.75 | 119.5 | 90 | Short separate CC2 escape. |
| R4 | 125 | 125 | 0 | Protected-rail LED current limiting near the indicator. |
| D1 | 131.5 | 125 | 180 | Indicator toward the bottom-right, outside the USB body. |

J2 pad 1 is +5V_PROTECTED at (134,106); pad 2 is GND at (130.5,106). Thus positive is the right terminal in this component-side view. J3 pads 1/3 form the left positive column at X=135.2; pads 2/4 form the right ground column at X=137.74. Row Y coordinates are 117 and 119.54. D1 cathode pad 1 is (131.5,125), and anode pad 2 is (128.96,125). Board polarity legends follow these rotations. The unkeyed header still requires mating-polarity checks; do not infer its orientation from the schematic drawing alone.

Rationale: actual rotation changes the physical presentation of the fixed pin contract without changing electrical polarity.

## Routing and operating restrictions

J1's two coincident VBUS contact groups escape separately to the back layer and join VBUS_RAW. U1 IN and active-high EN remain on VBUS_RAW; only U1 OUT feeds the common +5V_PROTECTED trunk and its J2, J3, C2 and R4 branches. Separate straight front-layer traces connect CC1/R1 and CC2/R2. The board uses routed back-layer returns rather than a ground plane. J1 shield/ground contacts are connected to GND. All six USB data/SBU terminals and U1 FLT remain intentionally unconnected as captured; no obsolete R3/ILIM_SET, pull-up or protection bypass was introduced.

Rationale: every external positive path and the indicator remain downstream of the common active switch; an electrically connected drawing does not demonstrate physical current capability.

Keep 4.75-5.25 V input, 500 mA TOTAL continuous external load with either connector independently usable, and strictly <2 mA externally unloaded VBUS as original requirements. The 0.831 mA conditional ledger is not measured or guaranteed. A known-capable source/cable must also supply overhead/startup. Outputs are load-only, with no backfeed or parallel supplies. Fault design must consider the 1.9 A static current-limit upper bound and unbounded dynamic overshoot, not a 500 mA source-current cap.

## Verification and preview evidence

- Baseline native DRC: clean for the stage with 26 unrouted connections and four J1 library-internal hole_clearance findings.
- Fresh v16 native run_drc after the actual placement/routing batch: clean for the original stage's placement/routing gate; four library-internal J1 hole_clearance findings remain separately listed. Fresh board readback confirms the outline and routes. No rule, suppression, pad or library geometry was changed.
- Separate supplied read-only KiCad 9.0.2 verification at 2026-10-08 22:49:42 UTC explicitly reports unconnected_items: [] (0). It returned exit code 5 because four intrinsic J1 hole_clearance errors remain, each actual 0.1944 mm against the unchanged 0.2500 mm board constraint. This independently executed check is not an original Copperhead tool result and is not a schematic-parity check; the parity flag was not requested.
- Board SHA-256 before/after that independent check: b07e3bfa0236ad11b54fbd4554b2cabb377a1cdee0bb4e1606a0f03e1e854470. Raw JSON SHA-256: 5a7523243f8b1345cb8be58443312f9ae983d1d7c4a80e95eef6c26ba1ea298f. The earlier interrupted run is historical only; all current placement, routing, native gates and this independent check were actually repeated in v16.
- Fresh run_erc and check_drift: clean. The schematic was not edited during Stage 5; Stage 4 symbol/legibility evidence and its inherited-U1 descriptive-metadata limitation remain as documented in BOM/PINOUT.
- Actual export_svg(kind=pcb) returned the project's .copperhead/renders directory. This records an executed preview export, not a visually inspected image or a completed fabrication package. Full original downstream export, firmware-applicability and bring-up stages remain pending.

## Draft quality

Fine for draft review: ten exact existing footprints are placed within the specified board envelope with edge-facing connector access, nearby bypass parts, separated CC traces, one common protected rail and explicit component-side output polarity. The fresh original native DRC gate, ERC and drift are clean, with the library-internal qualification below. Power and short functional nets have been routed, and the board explicitly says DRAFT - UNQUALIFIED.

Unrouted connections: 0, explicitly confirmed by the fresh independent KiCad JSON unconnected_items array on the unchanged current board, reduced from the native baseline of 26. The original native placement/routing DRC gate reports clean while separately retaining four intrinsic J1 hole_clearance findings. Raw KiCad exits 5 with those four errors at 0.1944 mm against the unchanged 0.2500 mm limit. Zero unrouted connections does not mean zero raw DRC findings, manufacturing readiness or physical qualification.

Library-internal findings: four J1 hole_clearance entries, explicitly classified by the original tool as inside a single library footprint and not placement problems. The fresh raw report identifies the J1 NPTH at (104.11,123.72) against the coincident A1/B12 ground pads at (103.8,122.645), and the NPTH at (109.89,123.72) against coincident A12/B1 ground pads at (110.2,122.645). Each reported clearance is 0.1944 mm versus the unchanged 0.2500 mm minimum. They are not fixed, suppressed or waived here. A PCB/library specialist and fabricator must review the exact connector drawing, slot/NPTH spacing, drilling capability and hole registration before fabrication. The stage's clean result does not mean raw DRC has zero findings.

What a human or specialist tool should redo/check before release:

1. Optimize the long, narrow ground-return topology and bypass loop areas, consider a properly cleared ground plane/thermal copper, shorten unnecessary detours, and verify all power necks/vias for 500 mA plus overhead and the current-limit/overshoot fault cases. The present layout is not thermally or transiently qualified.
2. Establish copper thickness and plating tolerances, loaded copper/contact voltage drop, source/cable interaction, and energy-limited sustained-short heating/recovery from exact TPS2065C evidence. Normal-load conduction loss is not proof of short-circuit safety.
3. Overlay exact J1/U1 manufacturer drawings; review J1 fine-pitch solder access, plug clearance, shell anchor strength, J2 wire/screwdriver access and torque support, J3 mating clearance/strain relief, LED assembly, and visible labels on the actual assembly. No connector fit or manual-assembly trial has occurred.
4. Obtain J3 finished plated holes within 0.97-1.07 mm, verify other holes/annuli and the four J1 internal findings, and keep the original manufacturing constraints. Nominal library drills are not guaranteed finished-hole tolerances.
5. Close capacitor effective-value/leakage, LED visibility and range-wide unloaded-current assumptions; execute the original electrical/thermal/orientation/polarity bring-up plan. No physical test is marked passed. Final Q100 quotations and header availability remain unverified.
6. Visually inspect the actual generated front/back/3D output and complete the original later export/applicability/bring-up pipeline. Draft gate success is not authorization to fabricate, procure or energize an unreviewed board.
